transfers.source_mechanism: Adaptive signal emission based on environmental feedback for target detection
transfers.target_problem: A maritime surveillance radar uses fixed LFM waveforms and suffers from excessive sea clutter false alarms. An adaptive waveform strategy is needed that adapts pulse duration to target range, reduces clutter false alarms, maintains resolution, and addresses range-Doppler coupling — all within real-time processing constraints on existing FPGA hardware.
transfers.transferred_principle: Adaptive waveform generation based on environmental feedback to enhance target detection while suppressing clutter
transfers.required_translation: Replace biological signal emission with radar pulse generation, substitute echo detection with clutter suppression algorithms, replace frequency adjustment with pulse duration modulation, and implement target classification through range-Doppler processing
transfers.expected_effect: Reduction in sea clutter false alarms while maintaining target detection performance through adaptive pulse duration based on target range
boundary_conditions: Waveform switching takes 1 ms (two pulse intervals)
failure_conditions: Signal interference from other radar systems
Range ambiguity due to pulse duration changes
Clutter masking in heavy sea states
transfers.testable_prediction: When implementing adaptive pulse duration based on target range, the system will achieve a false alarm rate of ≤10⁻⁶ per resolution cell per scan while maintaining detection probability ≥0.9 for 1 m² targets at 15 km in sea state 4
